summary: Rizick & Rizick CPAs is a two-principal boutique CPA firm at 57 Arizona Avenue in Old Bridge, NJ serving small businesses and individuals across Middlesex County, the NJ/NY metro area and remotely nationwide. Its service mix is unusually compliance-heavy for its size: outsourced accounting and bookkeeping, compilations and reviews, SOC 1 (SSAE 18) Type 1 and Type 2 internal-control audits, business valuation, and tax work including estate and gift returns. Client intake runs through a static web form or a single phone line, files move through a TaxDome portal (with a legacy ShareFile link still in the header), and the firm publishes no careers page or job postings.

facts.fact: Boutique, hands-on CPA firm located in Old Bridge, NJ; clients are primarily businesses and individuals in Middlesex County NJ, the NJ/NY metro area, and 'all over the U.S. virtually'; a high share of work is repeat/referral business and engagements can be conducted remotely or virtually.

Services: outsourced accounting and bookkeeping, financial statement preparation, compilations and reviews, business valuation, tax preparation (including estate and gift tax returns), audit and reporting services required under SSAE 18 for SOC 1 Type 1 and Type 2 reports, new-business advisory and QuickBooks setup/training.

Two named principals: Gail Rizick, CPA/ABV/CFF, CVA, ASA is the lead principal (business valuation and forensic accounting; CPA since 1990, CVA since 2001); Stuart Rizick, MBA, CPA, CGMA is the second principal.

SOC 1 practice is described as performing examinations of a service organization's controls over financial reporting and delivering SOC 1 Type 1 (description) and Type 2 (description plus testing) reports; example target clients cited include 401(k) recordkeepers and third-party administrators.

Address and channels: 57 Arizona Avenue, Old Bridge, New Jersey 08857; phone 732-387-0872; fax 732-640-5483; general email listed as gail@rizickcpas.com. No business hours are published on the contact page.

Consultation intake is a static web form (first/last name, phone, email, company name, 'how did you find us', mailing-list opt-in, free-text 'how can we help you', Google reCAPTCHA) that posts back to consultation.htm; the alternative offered everywhere is to call 732-387-0872. No calendar/online booking mechanism is present.

Client file transfer runs through a TaxDome portal file-request link (rizickrizickcpasllc.taxdome.com) labelled 'Send Us Files Securely'; the site header also still carries a ShareFile link (rizickrizickcpasllc.sharefile.com).
The site publishes roughly 30 client testimonials dated 2013 through November/December 2022, mostly attributed to business, individual tax and SOC 1 audit clients.
The About page links a 2024 peer review report PDF (/site_images/peer_review_report_2024r.pdf); the PDF is image-based and no readable findings text could be extracted.
Beyond QuickBooks, the firm advertises 'Profit 21/Epicor ERP System Software - setup, integration and accounting package consulting'.

The website is a static HTML site (18 URLs in sitemap, .htm pages) built and hosted by Build Your Firm marketing; page source shows Bootstrap 4.0.0, jQuery 3.3.1, a legacy Google+ publisher link, and a 2026 copyright line with no CMS or booking/chat widget.
The firm publishes a Content Library of 'hundreds' of tax and accounting articles across 10 categories, plus a newsletter sign-up and Tax Center/Tax Tips resource pages.

operations_signals: Client intake is two-channel only: a POST-back web form on consultation.htm (no confirmation of response time stated) or a phone call to the single main number 732-387-0872 (https://www.rizickcpas.com/consultation.htm).

No online scheduling/calendar tool is exposed anywhere on the site; every service page funnels to 'schedule phone consultation' or the phone number, so intake depends on manual call-back/email follow-up (https://www.rizickcpas.com/small-business-accounting-services.htm).
Contact page publishes street address, phone, fax and a principal's email but no hours of operation and no after-hours or emergency contact path (https://www.rizickcpas.com/contact.htm).

Service area is stated as Old Bridge/Middlesex County plus the New Jersey and New York metro area, with remote/virtual engagements for clients anywhere in the U.S. (https://www.rizickcpas.com/about-us.htm).

Document intake is handled through a TaxDome file-request portal, with a second, older ShareFile link still live in the mobile header - two overlapping client-file systems (https://www.rizickcpas.com/consultation.htm).

Workload is seasonal and deadline-clustered: individual, corporate, partnership, trust and estate returns plus e-filing (https://www.rizickcpas.com/income-tax-preparation-services.htm), alongside SOC 1 Type 2 examinations that require evidence collection and testing across an audit period (https://www.rizickcpas.com/soc1-audits.htm).

Firm markets scalability to businesses that do not want an in-house bookkeeper, i.e., it absorbs ongoing monthly bookkeeping/close work rather than only annual filings (https://www.rizickcpas.com/small-business-accounting-services.htm).

The published general email address is the lead principal's (gail@rizickcpas.com), implying front-door inquiries land with a principal rather than a dedicated intake coordinator (https://www.rizickcpas.com/contact.htm).
hiring_signals: No careers page exists: the sitemap lists 18 URLs (home, 8 service pages, about, testimonials, consultation, contact, newsletter, content library, privacy, peer review PDF) and none is a jobs or careers page (https://www.rizickcpas.com/sitemap.xml).

No live job postings for the firm could be confirmed; Indeed, LinkedIn, ZipRecruiter and Glassdoor company pages returned HTTP 403 / login walls and web search was unavailable during this session (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Rizick-%26-Rizick-Cpas).

Site language asserts staffing scale indirectly - 'tax professionals on staff' (https://www.rizickcpas.com/income-tax-preparation-services.htm) and client quotes repeatedly reference 'Gail and her team/staff', indicating at least a small support team around the two principals (https://www.rizickcpas.com/testimonials.htm).
review_themes: Responsiveness is the dominant praise theme: multiple client quotes describe prompt replies, quick answers and being 'very easy to get in contact with' (2013-2022) (https://www.rizickcpas.com/testimonials.htm).

Attention to detail and thoroughness recur, including one forensic-accounting client crediting the firm with uncovering irregularities and a bookkeeping client citing a significant error found after leaving a larger firm (https://www.rizickcpas.com/testimonials.htm).
Personal, principal-led service is repeatedly contrasted with 'chain' tax preparers; clients name Gail directly rather than the firm (https://www.rizickcpas.com/testimonials.htm).

Document logistics are praised for being easy and remote-friendly - clients mention emailing documents and being walked through what to deliver, which suggests the document-collection step is the client-facing friction point (https://www.rizickcpas.com/testimonials.htm).
Year-round planning and explanation quality (state multi-state returns, summary sheets explaining each part of the return) are cited as differentiators (https://www.rizickcpas.com/testimonials.htm).

No negative themes are observable: all quotes are firm-curated testimonials, the newest is late 2022, and no independent review platform (Google, Yelp, BBB) could be opened in this session (https://www.rizickcpas.com/testimonials.htm).
tech_footprint: Website: static .htm pages on Bootstrap 4.0.0 + jQuery 3.3.1, built and marketed by Build Your Firm (buildyourfirm.com); no CMS, no chat widget, no scheduling embed, dead Google+ publisher link (https://www.rizickcpas.com/consultation.htm).

Client portal / secure file exchange: TaxDome (rizickrizickcpasllc.taxdome.com file-request link) plus a residual ShareFile share link in the mobile header (https://www.rizickcpas.com/consultation.htm).

Lead capture: plain HTML form with Google reCAPTCHA and a mailing-list opt-in checkbox; sidebar duplicate 'Request a Consultation' form on interior pages (https://www.rizickcpas.com/consultation.htm).
Content/email: newsletter sign-up page and a syndicated-style Content Library of hundreds of articles plus Tax Center and Tax Tips sections (https://www.rizickcpas.com/content_library.htm).
Accounting software supported client-side: QuickBooks (setup, cleanup, training) and Profit 21/Epicor ERP (https://www.rizickcpas.com/quickbooks-accounting.htm).
Referral/review capture: footer links to a Build Your Firm 'Leave a Review' page rather than an embedded review widget (https://www.rizickcpas.com/consultation.htm).
No visible CRM, proposal/e-signature tool, client-status dashboard or AI/automation layer is exposed publicly (https://www.rizickcpas.com/sitemap.xml).
growth_signals: Compliance currency: a 2024 peer review report is posted publicly, which is the AICPA-required review cycle for firms performing attest work such as SOC 1 and reviews (https://www.rizickcpas.com/about-us.htm).

Service-line breadth has moved toward higher-value assurance and advisory (SOC 1 Type 1/2, compilations and reviews, valuations for estate/gift, M&A and litigation) rather than only 1040s (https://www.rizickcpas.com/our-accounting-services.htm).
Serves clients nationwide via remote engagements while keeping a single Old Bridge office - growth appears to come from reach rather than new locations (https://www.rizickcpas.com/about-us.htm).
Marketing investment is ongoing: Build Your Firm website plus newsletter and a large content library, indicating a referral-plus-inbound growth model (https://www.rizickcpas.com/content_library.htm).

No new locations, awards, press coverage or hiring announcements were found on the site; the most recent client testimonial is dated November/December 2022 (https://www.rizickcpas.com/testimonials.htm).
decision_maker: Gail Rizick, CPA/ABV/CFF, CVA, ASA - lead principal (https://www.rizickcpas.com/about-us.htm); second principal Stuart Rizick, MBA, CPA, CGMA

inferences.inference: Document chasing for annual returns and SOC 1 evidence is likely the largest recurring manual workload.
inferences.reasoning: The firm combines 1040/1065/1120/estate-and-gift preparation with SOC 1 Type 2 examinations that require tested evidence across a period, and clients themselves mention being guided through what documents to deliver; both are collection-and-follow-up heavy, and a two-principal firm has no visible dedicated intake staff.

inferences.inference: Missed-call and phone-tag leakage is a plausible revenue risk at intake.
inferences.reasoning: Every page routes prospects to a single phone number or a plain form with no scheduling, no published hours and no after-hours path; during tax season the same principal also prepares work, so inbound calls compete with billable production.

inferences.inference: The firm is mid-migration between file-sharing tools, which creates duplicate status tracking.
inferences.reasoning: TaxDome is the promoted modern portal, but a ShareFile share link is still in the site header, so staff may be reconciling documents across two systems.

inferences.inference: Firm size is roughly 3-8 people rather than the 10+ implied by the service mix.
inferences.reasoning: Two named principals, one office address, one main phone line, a principal's personal email as the public contact, and testimonials that say 'Gail and her team/staff' without naming other professionals; a larger attest practice would typically publish staff pages and a dedicated intake contact.

inferences.inference: The website is a low-maintenance marketing brochure rather than an operational system.
inferences.reasoning: Static .htm pages, a 2021-dated sitemap, legacy Google+ markup and no embedded booking, chat or client-status features indicate content is updated occasionally by the marketing vendor, not integrated with the practice.

inferences.inference: Growth is referral- and niche-driven, so capacity - not demand - is the constraint.
inferences.reasoning: The firm states a high percentage of business comes from repeat clients and referrals, advertises a differentiated SOC 1/valuation niche, and markets nationwide remote service; capacity is bounded by two principals' review time.

inferences.inference: Review evidence is thin and self-selected, so sentiment should be treated as marketing rather than measurement.
inferences.reasoning: All available reviews are firm-curated testimonials on the firm's own site with the newest from 2022; no independent Google/Yelp/BBB data could be accessed in this session.

data_gaps: No independent review data: Google Business Profile, Yelp, BBB, Yellowpages and Birdeye/Chamber listings were blocked (HTTP 403) or JavaScript-only; review themes here come from the firm's own testimonials page.

Hiring: no job postings verified. Indeed, LinkedIn, ZipRecruiter and Glassdoor all returned 403/login walls, and the web_search tool failed for every provider this session (Exa 429, OpenAI usage limit, no keys for Gemini/xAI/Mistral; DuckDuckGo, Bing, Brave and Mojeek fetches blocked or captcha'd).
Employee count and revenue: not published anywhere accessible; the mapper's employee range is an inference, not a sourced figure.
Firm founding year / years in business: not stated. Only principal credentials dates (CPA 1990, CVA 2001) are given.
Business hours and after-hours coverage: not published on the contact page.
Peer review report contents: the 2024 PDF is image-based, so pass/fail and scope could not be read - only its existence on the site is verified.
Pricing, fee structure, client counts and named client industries beyond examples in service pages: unknown.
LinkedIn company page (for size/headcount and recent posts) was inaccessible; no news, awards or press coverage could be searched.
